WelcomeTO OATLANDS SCHOOL
I feel extremely privileged to be the head of Oatlands, a school very much part of our community where staff, parents and the wider community work together to ensure that we provide the very best learning experiences for our children.
Our mission statement ‘Living our values, Learning for life’ is central to our ethos. Values lie at the heart of our curriculum and are fundamental in developing the Oatlands identity. As a school we ensure that all our pupils are happy, confident, inspired, independent learners. Our staff and children see every day as an opportunity, a chance to grow and a chance to learn. We believe that the journey as a life-long learner begins the moment a child starts at Oatlands.
We look forward to welcoming you to our school.
Tanya MooneyHead Teacher

Partnership
Manby Lodge Infant School, Oatlands Infant School and Cleves Junior School have a strong and beneficial partnership. There are close links between members of staff at all levels and the Governing Boards of each school also work in close collaboration.
Each year, our three schools work from a shared action plan with goals linked to academic achievement, curriculum, pastoral provision, and resourcing needs for children attending any of our schools.
Children at Oatlands or Manby Lodge Schools in year 2 have feeder status in Cleves’ Admissions Procedures. There is a structured programme to ensure that children moving from Year 2, at the end of Key Stage 1, to Year 3 in Cleves Junior School, have a smooth transition to KS2, or Junior School. This programme is overseen by the Deputy Headteachers and ensures that despite coming from two different Infant Schools, children are ready for the next stage in their learning journey, once they start Year 3. Our main focus this year, is ensuring that our over-arching 7-year curriculum, from the beginning of Year R to the end of Year 6, is progressive and structured logically and sequentially, and to make sure that there is good coverage within each subject. For more information on the 7-year curriculum journey please see subject specific curriculum overview grids here.
We strive for excellent outcomes for our children and we are all committed to working together in partnership to achieve this. Four specific shared priorities this year are:
- To identify all children’s SEND needs expeditiously; and to provide effective and prompt support to meet these needs
- To provide a rich and coherent 7-year curriculum journey for all children
- To boost and accelerate educational attainment, especially for low prior attainers
- For all 3 schools to have the financial resources they need to meet the needs of all their children

pageCache.text:
The Characteristics of Effective Learners
During their earliest years, children form attitudes about learning that will last a lifetime. Children who receive the right sort of support and encouragement during these formative years will be creative and adventurous learners throughout their lives. The Early Years Foundation Stage (EYFS) has identified three characteristics of effective teaching and learning.
Playing and exploring - children investigate and experience things, and ‘have a go’
Active learning - children concentrate and keep on trying if they encounter difficulties, and enjoy achievements
Creating and thinking critically - children have and develop their own ideas, make links between ideas, and develop strategies for doing things.
We have developed these into 10 ‘animal characters’ each with its own name and characteristic which the children can identify with, relate to and aspire to become. In class, teachers will reward evidence of these characteristics and them in order to promote positive attitudes and behaviours.
This can be reinforced at home when children are completing homework or undertaking practical tasks that they are unfamiliar with by using the animal names and promoting their positive characteristics.
If you would like to find out more about our animal friends or about the characteristics of effective learners, please speak to one of the reception teachers or have a look at the displays in school.

Sensory & Therapy Rooms
We are very fortunate to have both a sensory classroom and therapy room on site at Oatlands School. The therapy room is used by staff members and outside professionals to provide support for children with particular needs, for example occupational therapy, play therapy and sensory processing support.
Our sensory classroom enables children to journey far beyond Oatlands with its interactive floor, floor to ceiling projectors, surround sound, temperature control and scent diffusers. Classes regularly visit the sensory classroom and enhance their learning around a particular topic by immersing themselves in locations such as Victorian streets, the Kenyan savannah, snowy woodland and more. The room, which was generously funded by the school PTA, is also equipped with lighting and bubble tubes for children with additional needs to use as a quiet learning space.

Welcome From The Headteacher
Welcome to Oatlands School.
I feel extremely privileged to be the head of Oatlands, a school very much part of our community where staff, parents and the wider community work together to ensure that we provide the very best learning experiences for our children.
Our mission statement ‘Living our values, Learning for life’ is central to our ethos. Values lie at the heart of our curriculum and are fundamental in developing the Oatlands identity. As a school we ensure that all our pupils are happy, confident, inspired, independent learners. Our staff and children see every day as an opportunity, a chance to grow and a chance to learn. We believe that the journey as a life-long learner begins the moment a child starts at Oatlands.
We look forward to welcoming you to our school.
Tanya MooneyHead Teacher
At Oatlands, we are always interested in your feedback and are keen to find ways to improve all aspects of school life. We therefore encourage you to complete the Parent View Questionnaire every year so that we can keep on top of what we are doing well and what we could do better.
Please take some time to make us aware of your thoughts.
You can access the Parent View Questionnaire by clinking on the logo below.

Oatlands School PTA
Oatlands PTA is made up of parents and staff currently at Oatlands school. When your child joins Oatlands your family automatically become members of the PTA community, working together to organise a whole range of events across the school year. The money we raise from these events goes directly to benefit our children, by making our lovely school an even better place to learn, make friends and enjoy the experience of being at Oatlands.
While our main focus is to raise funds for the school through our events; we also have a key role to play in bringing the school community together socially. So, if you are new to Oatlands School or new to the Weybridge area, getting involved in the PTA will ensure that you meet lots or other Oatlands families and make some lifelong friends. The highlight of the school year for parents is often the Spring Ball where we all get dressed up and party hard! For the children, the Summer Funday, Sponsored Bounce and Dads & Kids Camping Weekend tend to feature in their top 3 annual school events however sometimes it's the termly bake sales, 2nd hand uniform sales or playground clean-up mornings that really show our community spirit and love for our school.
Organising all these fun activities takes some doing so while every parent and carer at Oatlands is a member of the PTA, we do have a committee of key individuals who carry out specific roles and make the magic happen. To find out more about the committee, please go to the main PTA website page by clicking here. Alternatively, you might wish to volunteer as a Class Rep; representing the parents of the children in your child's class and ensuring positive communication on key aspects of school life, or you may simply put your hand up every now and then to help on a stall at the Funday or sell some raffle tickets. Whatever you do it will be appreciated and will make a difference to the children at our school.
If time is an issue but you still want to help you can opt to donate to the PTA on a monthly basis via our Standing Order Contribution scheme (Friends of Oatlands - FOS). It is really easy and a great way of supporting the school financially while also enabling us to collect an additional 25% via the gift aid scheme. For more information about setting up a FOS standing order, please click here.
We really hope that you will come along and get involved when you join the school. We normally hold PTA meetings every 6 weeks or so on a Tuesday in the evening in the school hall, and everyone is welcome whether or not you have a role on the committee! Every year we look forward to welcoming new faces and this year, although strange, is no different!

Charity & Community
What's going on in our local community?
We are very lucky to be part of a thriving and active local community. We enjoy taking part in as many local community events as we can as a school and are happy to use our website to keep you informed about events and activities happening locally that you might like to take part in. Follow the links below to find out what's on in our community at the moment.
There are always lots of fun activities happening at St Mary's Oatlands. Please see the attachments at the bottom of this page for details of what's happening this month.
The foodbank have recently linked up with Kinship Carerswho are starting a new support group in Walton using our new space at The Bridge, Bridge Street, Walton.
A kinship carer is someone who is raising a family member or friends child and the group is to offer much needed support and friendship and is open to all.
For more information, please speak to Karen Hamilton at The Bridge on 07311 336 924 or by email at bridge@waltoncharity.org.uk
Please click HERE for more information on the new Space to Grow community space.
Please have a look at the flyers below for information on what fun & creative activities are happening at Chertsey Museum.
Throughout the school year, the children, staff and parents at Oatlands school will support a variety of local, national and international charities. Below is an overview of some of the charitable work we have done recently.
Please see the flyers below for information on either donating uniform or attending the Uniform Sale at The Bridge in
See the flyer below to Join the Mayor of Elmbridge for a walk, jog or run along the river to raise money for Elmbridge CAN and The Mayor of Elmbridge Trust Fund
Since 2011, we have been sponsoring 2 children via the Happy House (Children of Watamu) charity. Happy House provides a safe home for over 100 vulnerable children in Kenya as well as schooling for a further 380 children from nursery through to secondary school. We are currently sponsoring 2 girls: Diana and Elizabeth and receive regular updates about their progress and achievements. For more information about Happy House, please visit their website https://www.childrenofwatamu.net/
Each year, at our Harvest Festival, we collect food items for distribution to the local community foodbank. This year we supported both the Walton & Hersham and the Runnymede foodbanks (which covers the Weybridge area) with an amazing 186.85kg of donations. Thank you to all our wonderful Oatlands families for their incredible generosity. If you need support from the Foodbank please click here for more information.
We are proud to support the Royal British Legion Poppy Appeal each year selling poppies and other themed items in school.
